stances.claim: The SC merely held that the contested parcels (Parcels 3 and 4 Psu-2031, comprising 10 EMBO barangays) are part of Taguig's territory and that Taguig may exercise governance jurisdiction over them -- but the Court did NOT rule on ownership of any property within the parcels.
stances.rhetorical_move: doctrinal-clarification (separating territorial jurisdiction from proprietary ownership)

stances.claim: Taguig now exercises the governance powers and functions delegated to it by the Constitution and law -- taxation (especially real estate taxes), issuing/withholding business permits and licenses, and receiving its share of national-government revenues.
stances.confidence: asserted as direct effect of the ruling

stances.claim: National government functions remain unaffected by the territorial change -- VP Sara Duterte (DepEd) over schools, Sec. Benhur Abalos (DILG) over police, Sec. Teodoro Herbosa (DOH) over health all retain their supervisory powers regardless of which city the residents live in.

Proprietary rights (Makati's Torrens-titled ownership of the lands underneath the schools, hospitals, police stations, and fire stations it built and funded) subsist regardless of which city governs the political territory -- supporting Mayor Abby Binay's assertion of continued Makati ownership.
stances.rhetorical_move: Torrens-system framing (titles aren't extinguished by jurisdictional reassignment)

stances.claim: Residents' rights to vote and be voted for are not affected -- and Comelec can prevent confusion for the Oct. 30 barangay elections by ruling that previously-registered voters need not re-register; previously-filed COCs need not be re-submitted (with the caveat about serving Taguig barangays); existing precincts and polling places may be used.

The controversies 'need not deteriorate into confrontation and further confusion' -- with 'patience, reason, and logic,' the practical recommendations and doctrinal clarifications can resolve most disputes.
The proper virtues are 'humility from the victors and grace of acceptance from the vanquished' -- a litigation-disposition counsel applicable broadly, not only to this case.

notable_anecdotes: Roll-call of the 10 disputed barangays: Pembo, Comembo, Cembo, South Cembo, West Rembo, East Rembo, Pitogo, Rizal, Post Proper Northside, Post Proper Southside -- collectively known as Binay-family bailiwicks, adding political weight to the technical territorial ruling.

Inventory of Makati-funded facilities in the disputed parcels: public schools, Ospital ng Makati, Makati Science High School ('elite'), Fort Bonifacio High School, Makati City Jail, several police and fire stations -- establishing the practical stakes of the ruling.

Procedural marathon ('dizzying skirmishes in several RTC branches and appeals therefrom to several divisions of the Court of Appeals') compressed into one sentence -- emphasizing the doctrinal-stability cost of the long litigation.
Three Cabinet Secretaries named one-by-one (Sara Duterte/DepEd, Benhur Abalos/DILG, Teodoro Herbosa/DOH) to underscore that national-government supervision continues without interruption.
Mayor Abby Binay's name-cited assertion of Makati's continuing ownership rights -- used as confirming evidence rather than disputed claim.

Closing personal disclaimer ('I do not pretend to have absolute power or knowledge, only humble suggestions') paired with universal litigation counsel ('humility from the victors and grace of acceptance from the vanquished').

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban analyzes the Supreme Court Third Division's Dec. 1, 2021 decision in Makati v. Taguig (penned by Justice Ricardo R. Rosario with concurrence from JJ Leonen -- Division chair -- Carandang, Zalameda, and Marquez), which affirmed RTC Pasig Branch 153's July 8, 2011 ruling that Parcels 3 and 4 Psu-2031 of Fort Bonifacio -- comprising 10 barangays known as Binay-family bailiwicks (Pembo, Comembo, Cembo, South Cembo, West Rembo, East Rembo, Pitogo, Rizal, Post Proper Northside, Post Proper Southside) -- are part of Taguig's territory. The disputed area hosts public schools, Ospital ng Makati, the elite Makati Science High School, Fort Bonifacio High School, the Makati City Jail, and several police and fire stations, all built or funded by Makati. CJ clarifies that the SC merely ruled that Taguig now exercises governance jurisdiction (taxation including real estate taxes, business permits, national-government revenue share) -- but did not rule on ownership. National government functions remain unaffected: VP Sara Duterte (DepEd) over schools, Sec. Benhur Abalos (DILG) over police, Sec. Teodoro Herbosa (DOH) over health all continue their supervisory powers regardless of which city the residents live in. Proprietary rights are also not affected: if Makati holds Torrens-titled ownership of the lands and facilities it built and funded, that ownership 'subsists' -- supporting Mayor Abby Binay's assertion. Political rights of residents are likewise preserved; CJ then offers Comelec 'humble suggestions' to prevent confusion before the Oct. 30 barangay polls: voters already registered need not re-register; candidates who have filed COCs need not file new ones (with a caveat about now serving Taguig barangays); and existing precincts and polling places may be used. He closes with universal litigation counsel: with 'patience, reason, and logic,' confrontation can be avoided -- and 'I plead for the virtue of humility from the victors and for the grace of acceptance from the vanquished in this and in any other litigation.'
